quote: Population will increase by 1.2 billion to over 7 billion by 2010. About 95% of this growth will be in developing countries.

quote: Haiti's population, for example, is expected to double over the next 20 years.
note: Trend label: Haiti's population doubles in 20 years. 'Next 20 years' from 1997. Passive ('is expected'); source not named.

metric: world real per capita income growth, annual average 1997-2010
note: Trend label: Per capita income growth over 2 percent a year.

note: Trend label: Food production keeps pace with demand.

note: Trend label: Genetic engineering fuels a fourth agricultural revolution. 'This timespan' is to 2010.

note: Trend label: Added oil production equal to OPEC's 1997 output.

note: Trend label: Renewables do not significantly reduce fossil fuel reliance.

quote: no power will be able to match US battlefield technological capabilities during this time frame
note: Trend label: No power matches US battlefield technology.

quote: growth rates are projected at 2-3 percent per year at best
note: Trend label: European growth 2-3 percent a year at best. Europe section. Passive ('are projected').

quote: The likely course at least through 2010 will be an enlarged NATO serving as the primary vehicle for launching and sustaining "coalitions of the willing."
note: Trend label: Enlarged NATO the primary vehicle for coalitions.

note: Trend label: Political changes in Iran and Iraq by 2010. Parenthetical about Iran and Iraq in the Europe section.

note: Trend label: Russia economically weak through 2010.

note: Trend label: Russia too weak to project force beyond neighbors.

note: Trend label: China not the region's dominant military power.

note: Trend label: China-Taiwan unresolved; low risk of war.

note: Trend label: North Korea transformed; tensions eliminated. 'Next 15 years' from 1997.

note: Trend label: Southeast Asian disputes do not escalate into warfare. Context: overlapping claims to the Spratly Islands contested by China.

note: Trend label: Gulf oil producers fail to diversify.

note: Trend label: Saddam Husayn gone from Iraq.

note: Trend label: De facto Palestinian state by 2010.

quote: India will emerge as a major power economically, and remain a regional power militarily.
note: Trend label: India a major economic power, regional military power.

note: Trend label: India does not join CTBT or FMCT.

note: Trend label: Nigeria's problems unresolved for 15 years.

note: Trend label: South Africa a successful regional leader.

note: Trend label: PRI loses dominance in Mexico.

note: Trend label: No major Cuban reform while Castro in power.

quote: In this time frame, no country, no ideology, and no movement will emerge on a global scale to threaten US interests or to build and sustain an anti-Western coalition.
note: Trend label: No global anti-Western threat emerges. Implications section.

note: Trend label: Over three billion people in water-stressed regions. Overview, box 'Revisiting Global Trends 2010'.

note: Trend label: World population 7.2 billion in 2015. Overview, Demographics.

note: Trend label: 95 percent of population increase in developing countries. Overview, Demographics.

position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
note: Trend label: Food production adequate; malnourishment in parts of Sub-Saharan Africa. Overview, Natural Resources and Environment.

position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts

quote: The risk of war among developed countries will be low.
position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
note: Trend label: Low risk of war among developed countries. Overview, Future Conflict.

position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
note: Trend label: Internal conflicts stay at current levels or increase. Overview, Future Conflict.

note: Trend label: Rising likelihood of WMD use against the US. Overview, Future Conflict.

position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
note: Trend label: US influence unparalleled in 2015. Overview, Role of the United States.

position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
note: Trend label: Russia remains internally weak. Overview, Key Uncertainties: Russia.

position: projection; Global Trends 2015: A Dialogue About the Future With Nongovernment Experts
note: Trend label: India's population 1.2 billion by 2015. Overview, Key Uncertainties: India. The Discussion chapter says 'more than 1.2 billion'.

quote: A virtuous circle develops among technology, economic growth, demographic factors, and effective governance, which enables a majority of the world’s people to benefit from globalization.

note: Appendix, Scenario Two, p. 83. The global economy splits into three; WMD used in at least one internal conflict.

quote: Regional identities sharpen in Europe, Asia, and the Americas, driven by growing political resistance in Europe and East Asia to US global preponderance and US-driven globalization and each region’s increasing preoccupation with its own economic and political priorities.
note: Appendix, Scenario Three, p. 84.

quote: US domestic preoccupation increases as the US economy slows, then stagnates.
note: Appendix, Scenario Four, p. 84. US-European alliance deteriorates, US withdraws troops from Korea and Japan, Asian rivalries escalate toward a China-Japan crisis.

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: US remains single most powerful actor. 'The 2020 Global Landscape' table, relative certainties.

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: India's GNP overtaking European economies. Executive Summary. Which European economies is not stated.

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: Brazil and Indonesia approach European economies. Executive Summary. Hedged ('could').

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: North Korea crisis comes to a head within 15 years. Executive Summary. 'Next 15 years' from late 2004.

note: Trend label: Political Islam has significant global impact to 2020. Executive Summary, New Challenges to Governance.

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: Third wave of democratization may be partly reversed. Executive Summary. Hedged ('may').

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: Great power total war less likely than at any time in the past century. Executive Summary, Pervasive Insecurity. Also in the landscape table: 'Great power conflict escalating into total war unlikely.'

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: Nuclear states improve survivability and delivery systems. Executive Summary.

note: Trend label: al-Qa'ida superseded by similar groups by 2020. Executive Summary, Transmuting International Terrorism. 'superceded' is as printed.

position: projection; Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
note: Trend label: Terrorist attacks mainly with conventional weapons. Executive Summary.

quote: Davos World provides an illustration of how robust economic growth, led by China and India, over the next 15 years could reshape the globalization process—giving it a more non-Western face and transforming the political playing field as well.
note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 1.

quote: Pax Americana takes a look at how US predominance may survive the radical changes to the global political landscape and serve to fashion a new and inclusive global order.
note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 2.

note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 3.

note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 4.

note: Trend label: EU, not NATO, becomes Europe's primary institution. Executive Summary, Policy Implications ('Some trends we probably can bank on').

note: Trend label: Terrorism unlikely to disappear by 2025. Relative certainty, table p. iv.

note: Trend label: Post-WWII international system almost unrecognizable by 2025. Executive Summary, p. vi.

note: Trend label: Sub-Saharan Africa remains most vulnerable region. Executive Summary, p. vii.

note: Trend label: Many Latin American major countries middle income by 2025; Haiti poorer. Executive Summary, p. vii.

note: Trend label: Risk of nuclear weapon use greater than today. Executive Summary, p. x. 'Next 20 years' from 2008.

position: projection; Global Trends 2025: A Transformed World
note: Trend label: No dominant political identity by 2025. Executive Summary, p. xi.

position: scenario; scenario Politics is Not Always Local
note: Executive Summary, p. xii. Body: a nonstate coalition helps elect the UN Secretary General and secures a new worldwide climate agreement.

note: Trend label: World population close to 8.3 billion. Megatrend 3, p. iii.

note: Trend label: Nearly half of world population under severe water stress. Tectonic Shifts table, p. v.

note: Trend label: Islamist phase of terrorism might end by 2030. Game-Changer 3, p. viii. Hedged ('might').

quote: Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Central America, and the Caribbean will remain vulnerable, nevertheless, to state failure through 2030
note: Trend label: Sub-Saharan Africa, Central America, Caribbean vulnerable to state failure. Game-Changer 4, p. ix.

quote: by 2030 many leading centers of innovation in disease management will be in the developing world.
note: Trend label: Leading disease-management innovation centers in the developing world. Game-Changer 5, p. x.

quote: The US most likely will remain “first among equals” among the other great powers in 2030 because of its preeminence across a range of power dimensions and legacies of its leadership role.
note: Trend label: US 'first among equals' in 2030. Game-Changer 6, p. x.

note: Trend label: Next five years: rising tensions, slower global growth. The Future Summarized, p. ix. 'Next five years' from January 2017.
